target_customer: Latin American gig platforms, fintechs, banks and HR teams that need background checks and identity verification
problem: Background checks in Latin America took days to weeks and cost around $30 per person, which blocked fast onboarding for gig workers and customers.
business_model: Usage based API and web services for background checks, identity verification and fraud prevention
product_category: Identity verification and background check API

founders.name: David Cuadrado
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page; background from TechCrunch 2022-04-08.

founders.name: Cesar Pino
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page; background from TechCrunch 2022-04-08.

founders.name: Bruno Cecatto
founders.background_notes: Named a co-founder in the Magma Partners Q&A; not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Traditional Latin American background check providers
competitors.what: Manual background screening that took up to a week and cost about $30 per person
competitors.traction_then: Incumbent practice; no named vendor in the source

technical_complexity.rationale: Aggregating court, police and identity records across several countries and doing ID scanning and verification needs many integrations, but the stack is standard API engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Country by country data integrations, certifications and API embedding in customer onboarding flows are slow to replicate, but KYC is crowded.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought the wedge in sources found; Truora itself acquired Brazilian e-signature firm ZapSign in 2022.

market_need_then: Gig platforms such as Rappi, Uber and Davivienda were early customers (latamlist 2019-06), and the founders pitched them before building to confirm demand (Magma Partners Q&A).

branding.domain_note: Uses truora.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.visual_style: B2B product site with customer logos and ISO certifications
identity.voice_and_tone: Professional trust and security tone in Spanish

brand_strength.rationale: A B2B API brand known through funding press and customer logos; no brand-specific press, community or merch found.

pivots.to: Broader identity verification, fraud prevention and WhatsApp onboarding
pivots.why: Expand from background checks into a digital trust platform; later products include e-signature and reusable identity

outcome_analysis: Truora started with background checks for gig platforms, raised a seed from Magma and MAYA before YC, then a $3.5M seed and a $15M Series A at $75M post-money in 2022 with Accel and Kaszek. It grew to about 80 to 110 staff, added ID verification and e-signature through the ZapSign purchase, and remains active; no later priced round was found.
notes: Seed investors conflict across sources: Magma Partners and MAYA in 2018-12 (Magma Q&A), Magma 2019-06 (latamlist), Accel and Kaszek co-led $3.5M seed (TechCrunch); the two seed rows may overlap and the TechCrunch seed date is stated only as March after YC. Founding date June vs August 2018 conflicts. Founder education not found in opened sources. Outcome search found no shutdown or layoffs for Truora. Competitors: no named rivals in dated sources; Emptor (Peru, founded 2016) exists but its source is undated.
